wi_hillbilly_routes.blurb: Hillbilly Hollow is a small sandstone bluff tucked behind a highway rest stop near Coloma in central Wisconsin, and the Hillbilly Routes are its main climbing. Our catalog holds 44 climbs, about half bolted, nearly as many on gear, and a few top-ropes. Grades start around 5.5 and run into the 5.12s with a single 5.13, but most lines sit between 5.7 and 5.10. Expect short, friction-dependent faces and slabs with sharp patina holds, so it makes a handy change of pace from Devil's Lake. The bluff is right beside a public rest area, so keep a low profile and stay quiet. Easy, brief walk from the car.
wi_hillbilly_routes.parking_note: Leave the car at the highway rest area near Coloma; the bluff sits just behind it.
wi_hillbilly_routes.approach: A short, easy walk from the rest area to the base of the bluff.

wi_1_old_sandstone.blurb: Old Sandstone is a cliff on the east side of the Baraboo Range near Devil's Lake, set apart from the park's better-known quartzite bluffs. The sandstone has rounded edges, embedded pebbles and good friction, with blank slabs and curving cracks, and the wall reaches roughly 65 feet at its tallest. Most of our 42 climbs are traditional, with a good number of top-rope lines and a couple of boulder problems. Grades run from easy 5.4 to low 5.12, bunched around 5.9 and 5.10. Devil's Lake has no fixed bolts or anchors, so bring a rack. Parking is small, and the area is growing in popularity.
wi_1_old_sandstone.parking_note: Dirt pull-off on the south side of the road, about 1.25 miles east of the CCC lot and just before the back of a 35 MPH sign. It fits roughly four cars.
wi_1_old_sandstone.approach: Cross the road, pick up the trail beside the speed limit sign, and hike up the forested slope until it flattens and the cliff appears on your right.

wi_balanced_rock_wall.blurb: Balanced Rock Wall is a wall of about 40 feet on the East Bluff at Devil's Lake State Park, right beside the Balanced Rock Trail. It is among the park's busiest spots, so expect company and plenty of hikers watching. Of our 37 climbs, most are traditional, nine are top-rope, and two are boulder problems. Grades run from very easy up to 5.13, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.11 range. The quartzite is hard and the ratings run stiff. There are no permanent bolts or anchors, so it is gear or top-rope. The access is short and simple, and the rock is said to dry quickly in a breeze.
wi_balanced_rock_wall.parking_note: Use the South Shore lot at the lake, then walk up the Balanced Rock Trail from the picnic area.
wi_balanced_rock_wall.approach: Follow the Balanced Rock Trail up rock steps to about the halfway point of the bluff; the wall is right at the trail.
